title: security: rbac v2 - enforce KMS region pinning + audit logging enhancements
author: Asha Patel
description:
This PR implements enforcement for KMS region pinning in RBAC v2 policies and adds richer audit logging for KMS-related operations. Motivation: customers with data residency requirements need guarantees that keys bound to a resource are region-restricted and that any policy changes or uses of cross-region keys are auditable. This change closes gaps surfaced in SEC-1124 and ENG-8421 and is needed for upcoming Private deployments with strict residency controls.

What this PR does: 
- Adds policy schema fields and validation to RBAC v2 to allow specifying kms_region and kms_residency_policy on KeyBinding and SecretBinding resources. Validation occurs at admission time in the control plane and at serve-time policy evaluation for dedicated/private modes.
- Enforces region pinning: when a resource requires a pinned region, any referenced KMS key must be in the same region or be explicitly allowed by an account-level residency exception.
- Enhances audit logging: KMS audit events now include key_id, key_region, policy_id, requester_identity, evaluated_policy_version, and an explicit reason field when an operation was rejected due to residency. Logs are structured and tagged so downstream SIEMs can create residency alerts.
- Adds migration path and feature flag: changes are gated by feature flag `rbac_v2_kms_region_enforcement`. Default rollout is audit-mode (log-only) for two weeks, then enforced. A migration job will scan existing bindings and emit findings to the compliance queue.
- Tests and docs: unit tests for policy validation, integration tests exercising enforcement and exception flows, and docs describing the new schema and migration steps.

Checklist included in the body: 
- [x] Schema changes and validation 
- [x] Serve-time checks and admission webhook updates 
- [x] Audit log schema and logging hooks 
- [x] Migration job and compliance queue producer 
- [x] Unit + integration tests 
- [x] Docs and migration guide under docs/security/rbac-v2-kms-region-pinning.md 

Compatibility and rollout notes: 
- Default behavior after merge: feature flag set to `audit-only` in main; ops will flip to `enforce` after monitoring for 14 days. Customers on Dedicated/Private can opt into earlier enforcement.
- Backwards compatibility: existing policies without kms_region continue to behave as before under audit-only. A migration job will create recommended kms_region values where possible (based on resource telemetry).
- Operational impact: there is a small latency impact on admission validation (~2-5ms per request) due to extra validation and cache lookups; we added cache TTLs and batched lookups to mitigate.

Rollout plan: 
1. Merge to main in audit-only mode. 
2. Run migration scan and surface findings to compliance queue. 
3. Monitor for false positives and performance impact. 
4. After 14 days, flip to enforcement in staging, then prod.

If enforcement causes mass failures, the feature flag and an emergency bypass RBAC role exist to quickly revert enforcement for affected tenants.

References: SEC-1124, ENG-8421. Linear cards linked.

Lin Chen: Audit schema looks good. Suggest adding a machine-readable `residency_reason` code in addition to the human-readable reason so SIEM rules can match reliably.

release_notes:
- Enforce KMS region pinning for RBAC v2 policies (feature-flagged: rbac_v2_kms_region_enforcement).
- Audit logs for KMS now include key_id, key_region, evaluated_policy_version and residency_reason.
- Migration job to help identify bindings that need kms_region values.
- Default rollout in audit-only mode for 14 days, then opt-in enforcement for Dedicated/Private customers.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag on/off via console or use env REDWOOD_FEATURE_RBAC_V2_KMS_REGION. Migration job: redwood-tools/migration/kms_region_scan --output compliance-queue. If enforcement causes failures, grant role `residency-bypass` or flip feature flag. Monitor metric residency_reject_count and admission_latency_ms.
security_impact: Medium. Introduces stricter enforcement of key residency constraints which improves compliance posture. Requires careful rollout to avoid service impact for tenants using cross-region key setups.
qa_summary: Unit tests cover schema validation and residency_reason codes. Integration test validates enforcement path and exemption flows. Ran e2e in staging against a dataset of 200 bindings; expected findings surfaced and no unexpected rejects in audit-only mode.
